title: Cross-Cloud Resource Tagging Compliance

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.4.26 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.4.26 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:config:notification` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Policy exports, GCP Asset Inventory; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
app: `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Policy exports, GCP Asset Inventory
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" (  configRuleName="*tag*" complianceType="NON_COMPLIANT")

description: A single tagging schema across clouds enables chargeback and policy automation; drift in one provider breaks consolidated FinOps views.
value: Detecting cross-cloud resource tagging compliance early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Normalize required tag keys (for example Environment, Owner, CostCenter) in a lookup. Weekly trend of non-compliant count per provider. Alert when any provider’s gap exceeds SLA threshold.
visualization: Stacked bar (non-compliant by provider over time), Table (resource, missing tags), Single value (compliance %).

| tstats `summariesonly` count

dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Change (All_Changes).
knownFalsePositives: Our own break-glass and automation accounts show up the same as anyone else, and a delete or write during a change window is expected. We allowlist the roles that do routine maintenance and we link alerts to approved changes before we call an incident.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Policy exports, GCP Asset Inventory with the modular input for `aws:config:notification`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.4.33.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Normalize required tag keys (for example Environment, Owner, CostCenter) in a lookup. Weekly trend of non-compliant count per provider. Alert when any provider’s gap exceeds SLA threshold.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:config:notification" (  configRuleName="*tag*" complianceType="NON_COMPLIANT")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.4.26_cross_cloud_resource_tag_26"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:config:notification` in `index=aws` to detect cross-cloud resource tagging compliance. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_4_26_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Stacked bar (non-compliant by provider over time), Table (resource, missing tags), Single value (compliance %)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws`, Azure Policy exports, GCP Asset Inventory and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of cross-cloud resource tagging compliance so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
